findings.title: Theme B observability hook has no concrete injection point and its stated location inverts the downward-only dependency rule
findings.where: §7B vs. the concrete tools.py listing in §4.1; §1 dependency-direction statement
findings.problem: FR-6.1 / Acceptance Criterion 10 require per-step traces (latency, tools called, token/step counts). §7B names a 'lightweight wrapper around tool calls' but the only concrete orchestration/tools.py listing (§4.1) shows bare module-level @tool functions with no span, timing, or wrapper, and §4.2 hands those un-wrapped tools to the agent. The injection mechanism (in-body span vs Strands callback vs decorator) is unspecified, and the stated wrapper location (orchestration/tools.py calling concierge/observability.py) creates an orchestration->concierge dependency that contradicts the §1 'dependencies point downward only: application -> orchestration' rule, which is the architecture-diagram slide (NFR-5).
findings.fix: Add a concrete code block showing the wrapper as a contextlib.contextmanager span(name, **fields) that records start/end/duration_ms and emits one JSON line when enabled, no-ops when disabled (preserving the no-network eval, FR-6.4), and is stdlib-only so tools stay importable without Strands (INV-9). Tie per-step step_count to the number of tool.* spans. Place the span/no-op primitive in a module orchestration may legally depend on (or explicitly amend the §1 dependency-direction statement) so the architecture claim is not silently inverted.

findings.title: Eval check numbering (§6) does not map one-to-one to the named functions (§5A)
findings.where: §6 ten-row table vs §5A function names (contract 1-4, scoring 5-9, version 10)
findings.problem: §6 check #5 ('System prompt contains no source ids') is the same thing as §5A scoring check #5 test_prompt_carries_no_structure, but the §6 numbers are not annotated with owning module/function, making it easy to misimplement as two separate prompt checks.
findings.fix: Annotate each §6 table row with its owning module + function name (e.g. row 5 -> scoring.test_prompt_carries_no_structure; row 10 -> contract_checks.test_version_consistent) so the ten numbered checks map unambiguously to the nine named functions plus the version check.

findings.title: Deterministic-eval quality_score is over fixed synthetic answers, not stated plainly
findings.problem: In the deterministic eval there is no agent answer; scoring predicates run over fixed synthetic candidate answers, so quality_score is constant per {layer_version}+fixtures. Adequate for FR-6.2 but a reader could expect it to reflect live model quality and wire a model call into the deterministic record, breaking INV-4/NFR-2.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: in the deterministic eval quality_score is computed over fixed synthetic answers and is stable per {layer_version}, changing only when the layer version or fixtures change; live model quality is recorded only on the optional --model path.

findings.title: 'No reload needed' is true only for data-only Beat 4; adding a new source needs reload + platform rebuild
findings.problem: The 'reload is unnecessary' claim holds for the scripted data-only Beat 4 (new CSV rows re-read each query_source call). But the stronger add-a-new-source path (new schema.json/sources.md entry, FR-1.2/AC5) does require _LAYER.reload() AND rebuilding _PLATFORM, because _PLATFORM/_LAYER are built once at module import from the cached schema; an in-process live add silently won't take effect. The design never states this.
findings.fix: Clarify in §5E: data-only edits need no reload; adding a new source requires _LAYER.reload() plus rebuilding _PLATFORM from the refreshed schema (in practice a process restart). Note the demo's Beat 4 avoids this by staying data-only and the §11 extensibility test builds a fresh platform per run, so Acceptance Criterion 5 stays honest.
